arguments.prompt:
Create a FOUR-POSE animation sprite sheet by editing this exact existing California Towhee individual. Preserve the same detailed naturalistic pixel-art bird identity, same brown warm gray body, subtle rust face/chin and rust undertail, plain unstriped breast, dark eye and short chunky gray conical seed bill, long plain brown tail, pinkish-brown legs. Preserve quiet small pixel clusters and nuanced feather pattern. Do not introduce black/orange Spotted Towhee plumage, new markings, altered proportions, cartoon outline, tiny detached feathers, props or scenery. Bird faces RIGHT throughout. Real new body-and-leg poses, not whole-bird translations of a standing pose.

Make EXACTLY FOUR equal SQUARE cells in a TWO-by-TWO atlas: top-left crouch; top-right airborne; bottom-left descending; bottom-right supported settle. Transparent RGBA background. No words, panel borders, ground line, cast shadow or extra birds. Keep every entire bird/tail/toe visible within its own cell with generous transparent margins. Use the SAME source camera and SAME individual scale for ALL four cells. A neutral source bird is provided as the scale/anatomy reference, not an extra atlas panel. The whole sheet should use one consistent perspective and size. Use a virtual support/root point around x59%,y79% within each cell. Crouch and settle toes sit on the SAME ground plane at y79%; leave the ground visually transparent. Body pose may compress or rise naturally, but not resize or change bird identity.

This is a modest BACKWARD ground hop while still facing right, characteristic of a ground-foraging towhee. Screen travel is applied later by code, so DO NOT place different cells farther left/right. Each cell has the same local root/camera. Wings stay neatly folded; do not turn this into flight. No leaf scratching props; this is only one hop, not a complete double-scratch behavior.

TOP LEFT, CROUCH/COMPRESSION: pelvis/body a little lower than the neutral, legs clearly flexed, both feet firmly spread on the support baseline, torso compresses plausibly in preparation for springing backward; head alert facing right, tail helps balance.
TOP RIGHT, AIRBORNE TUCK: distinctly lifted/rounded springing body pose with both lower legs folded underneath and toes visibly curled/tucked up away from the ground. Two anatomically clear legs/feet; no planted toe or support contact. Tail adjusts modestly for balance. Keep body size unchanged and feet fully visible.
BOTTOM LEFT, DESCENDING/REACHING: different body pitch and BOTH legs extending down toward the landing plane, toes opening to meet the ground; still airborne, toes slightly above support line, no toe dragged behind or rigid duplicate standing pose. Distinct leg extension compared with tucked airborne frame.
BOTTOM RIGHT, SUPPORTED SETTLE: both feet planted on y79% again, with knee/ankle flex and a slightly forward settling chest absorbing the landing; wings folded, no flight or extra limbs. This must be a real distinct landing-body drawing, not an identical neutral copy.

At small game size the actual bird is about78world units long. Favor clear leg states and recognizable silhouette at that size; exact source pixel equality is not required. Consistent anatomy/scale and believable planted versus airborne contact matter more than microscopic feather changes. All four poses will be exported without per-pose fitting.
